basis: per kg of hydrogen cyanide, Tab. 43.2 / 43.3 / 43.4 of chapter 43 of ecoinvent report No. 8 (Althaus et al. 2007), all printed per kg or per kg in grams
allocation: None stated. The chapter reports three co-products per kg HCN - 0.23 kg hydrogen (BMA route, if not burnt), 0.34 kg ammonium sulfate sold as fertiliser and 0.02 kg sodium cyanide - but gives no allocation factor, so every burden below stays with the HCN.

items.name: Ammonia
items.note: Tab. 43.2 'Resource consumption for the production of HCN (kg/kg)'; the feedstock of both the Andrussow and the BMA route (2 NH3 + 2 CH4 + 3 O2 -> 2 HCN + 6 H2O).

items.name: Natural gas, feedstock
items.factor_source: lower heating value of natural gas 45.4 MJ/kg (ecoinvent v2 convention); cross-checked against the same chapter's 'A total of 31 MJ is required per kg of HCN', which is 0.68 kg x 45.4 MJ/kg = 30.9 MJ
items.note: Tab. 43.2, the methane fed to the reactor (2 NH3 + 2 CH4 + 3 O2 -> 2 HCN + 6 H2O). Printed in kg; every natural-gas supply dataset in BAFU is in MJ, so the printed kg is converted with the standard heating value.

items.name: Sulfuric acid (conc.)
items.note: Tab. 43.2. Used to scrub the unreacted ammonia; consistent with the solid-waste line '0.34 kg of ammonium sulfate ... are produced per kg of HCN'.

items.name: Natural gas, process fuel
items.factor_source: lower heating value of natural gas 45.4 MJ/kg (ecoinvent v2 convention; cross-check with the same chapter's 'A total of 31 MJ is required per kg of HCN', which equals 0.68 kg x 45.4 MJ/kg)
items.note: Tab. 43.3 'Energy consumption for the production of HCN (kg/kg)' gives two columns, 'Hydrogen export route' 0.78 and 'Hydrogen combustion route' 0.51. The point estimate is the combustion route because Tab. 43.4's air emissions are stated to belong to it: 'These figures ... are calculated values based on the combustion of hydrogen gas in the process as a fuel that replaces part of the natural gas burned as a fuel.' The two columns are the printed range, so the amount is calibratable between them. Mapped to a heat-from-natural-gas dataset because BAFU has no 'natural gas burned' dataset in kg; the MJ of gas is charged as MJ of heat, which understates the gas by the furnace efficiency (~10 %). Flagged medium.

items.name: Total process energy
items.quote: A total of 31 MJ is required per kg of HCN.
items.note: Cross-check only, not a separate input: 31 MJ is the same energy as the natural-gas lines above (0.68 kg x 45.4 MJ/kg = 30.9 MJ). Counting it again would double the fuel.

items.name: Dust (SPM)
items.note: Tab. 43.4 'Air emissions from the production of HCN (g/kg)', BMA process.

items.name: SOx
items.note: Tab. 43.4. Printed as SOx; mapped to sulfur dioxide, the ecoinvent/EF convention for SOx reported as a single figure.

items.name: CO2
items.note: Tab. 43.4 = 2.474 kg CO2 per kg HCN, against 4.69 kg in the cumulated vector of the same chapter, so about half the dataset's CO2 is direct - a plausible split for a fired reactor.

items.name: Hydrogen
items.quote: In case the hydrogen produced by the BMA process is not combusted, a total of 0.23 kg hydrogen is produced per kg HCN.
items.note: Co-product of the BMA route only, and only when not burnt in the process. The point estimate chosen for the fuel line above is the combustion route, in which this hydrogen is consumed internally, so it is recorded as a co-product but not credited.

items.name: Ammonium sulfate
items.quote: 0.34 kg of ammonium sulfate (Na2SO4) are produced per kg of HCN, as well as 0.02 kg of sodium cyanide. The ammonium sulfate is sold as a fertilizer.
items.note: Sold as fertiliser, so an economic co-product; the report gives no allocation factor, and none is applied here (all burdens stay with HCN). Note the report's own formula slip: ammonium sulfate is (NH4)2SO4, not Na2SO4.

items.name: Sodium cyanide
items.quote: as well as 0.02 kg of sodium cyanide
items.note: Listed under solid wastes; no allocation given.

gaps: Electricity: not mentioned anywhere in the excerpt, although the Andrussow reactor, the ammonia absorber and the HCN stripper all need it.
Process water and cooling water: not given ('Wastewater / Liquid wastes: No values available.').

Water emissions: the excerpt states outright that no values are available, yet the aggregated dataset carries water emissions; those necessarily come from the upstream chain in the cumulated original.

Infrastructure (chemical plant) and feedstock transport: not mentioned; ecoinvent's own convention for this family (4.0E-10 units of 'chemical plant, organics', 0.6 tkm rail + 0.1 tkm lorry per kg of precursor) is a BAFU template, not something this excerpt prints.

The Andrussow/BMA split: the excerpt says only 'BMA accounts for 15 % of the total European production', and Tab. 43.2/43.3/43.4 do not say which route each column belongs to except for Tab. 43.4 (BMA).
Oxygen / air for the Andrussow route (equation 1) is not quantified.
The catalyst (platinum gauze) is described qualitatively and never quantified.
